targets.observation: 2026-10-31: in the accepted text_palette_e3b8 context f_e074 is size-exact at its nominal root (808 bytes) but only 87 bytes equal. ROM frame 24 keeps run=1 on the stack @(16) and hoists f_2bf58 into r13; the context keeps run in r11 (frame 20) and reloads f_2bf58 per call. Same pattern as startup f_780 (ROM hoists f_e3e0/f_e520/f_185f0 and spills loop locals). ROM registers r9=g_606006c base (pool 0606006c, displacement fields @(8)/@(4), b28 via r0), r13=f_2bf58, r14=g_6032ff8, r10=320, and reloads f_2b4e8 at each call; context folds field addresses (06060074/06060070), hoists f_2b4e8 in r10 and keeps run in r11. f_bc02 (code-exact, same extern array) also keeps the unfolded base in a register, so the difference is leaf-web priority, not declaration. Sort capture (research/2026-10-31-textmenu-sort, 12 stages, native-equal): the draft's register buttons has priority 65541 and drives every clashing web's profit to about -1370. Without register (research/2026-10-31-textmenu-noregister) f_e074 takes the ROM opening (run on stack, f_2b4e8 reloaded, base table in r14) at 806 bytes vs 808; remaining: hoisted &h[0]/&h[1] stack temps (frame 32 vs 24). short i/sel reproduce ROM exts.w caching but give 814 bytes; block-local h has no effect. The no-register draft hoists &h[0]/&h[1] (mov r15,r2; add #28) out of while(run) into stack temps; ROM stores h[0]/h[1] directly @(20)/@(22) and recomputes r15+20 inside the j loop (e1d2), i.e. &h is never treated as loop-invariant. asm/00d394.s marks 0xe16a as a function entry, but it is inside f_e074. Unresolved drafts still declaring register locals: f_274c0, f_7324, f_2ac4c, f_7fa0, f_be28, f_21d94, f_f29a, f_f3a2 (register priority +65536 distorts allocation). ROM never propagates run=1: it branches to the loop test first (bra e37e) and rereads run @(16,r15); the draft enters the body directly and hoists &h, table pointers and constants. Diagnostic volatile run (research/2026-10-31-textmenu-run-diagnostic, not admissible) keeps the &h hoisting and frame 32 (size 814), so run propagation is not the switch. Switch dispatch identical in ROM and draft (compare chains on sel, no jump tables), so dispatch shape does not explain the unhoisted original loop. h shape solved: an array h hoists &h[0]/&h[1] for its constant-index stores; a two-short struct (h.a/h.b stored directly, loop indexes ((short*)&h)[j]) gives ROM's direct stores and inline loop base (research/2026-10-31-textmenu-h-struct-diagnostic). Adding short i/sel gives ROM frame 24 with run @(16) and h @(20)/(22), size 794 (research/2026-10-31-textmenu-struct-short). Outer-loop hoisting: volatile run (diagnostic only) still hoists; a goto-built outer loop reproduces ROM entry (bra to bottom test, sel=0 in delay slot), per-pass reloads and base+displacement stores, but frame 16 and 766 bytes (research/2026-10-31-textmenu-goto-loop). Unprototyped externs do not change argument order (identical object). A static #pragma inline helper center(s,y){f_2bf58(s,y,(320-f_2c0d0(s))>>1);} (same unit family as f_9c0c's #pragma inline helpers; not emitted standalone, matching ROM) reproduces ROM's label/y spills around f_2c0d0: 780 bytes, raw 664, frame 20 (research/2026-10-31-textmenu-inline-center/center.c, current best). Sort capture of center.c (research/2026-10-31-center-sort, 12 stages, native-equal): g_606006c leaf 5/r13, f_2bf58 4/r12, sel 4/r11, const64 4/r10, d_3aa9c leaf 3/r9, const0 1/none, const320 -1/none; ROM registers 320 (r10) and 0 (r11) but not d_3aa9c. ROM loads 0x3aa9c afresh at e0b0/e13c and a folded 0x3aac0 for entry [1]; numeric-cast tables (research/2026-10-31-textmenu-numeric-tables) give 778 bytes and raw 670: rejected. center.c post-allocation tree: the d_3aa9c leaf web is materialised as lreg8 = d_3aa9c at its first use (initial object stores, line 123) and stays live function-wide in r9; ROM uses a temporary r4 for those stores and reloads per pass, so the original leaf web is split at, or never formed across, the outer loop. A local menu pointer is contradicted by ROM's folded 0x3aac0 for entry [1]. Inner loops: goto-built i/j loops (research/2026-10-31-textmenu-inner-goto/innergoto.c, 16 stages) put d_3aa9c, (long)sel and (long)i in the i-loop test block as ROM e13c..e14e does, and i=0/j=0 copy the const-0 register: 790 bytes (from 780). Remaining: ROM registers 64 (r8) and 320 (r10) where the draft registers 1 and 3; ROM spills the d_3aa9c element pointer @(8); the draft cross-jumps the two sel==2 centered-label tails that ROM keeps separate (then-branch scheduled differently). A void* vs char* helper parameter is byte-identical (research/2026-10-31-textmenu-center-charp, 8 stages, prediction failed). The b&0x20 cases form the incremented field in short c before reducing it (c = (g & m) + 1; c %= n;): ROM and/add #1/exts.w order into the modulo call, constants 1/3 no longer function-wide registers, run=0 and i/j=0 via r11 as ROM; 794 bytes, raw 510, 220 of 404 opcodes exact (research/2026-10-31-textmenu-modulo-short/modshort.c, current best). Native sort capture of modshort.c (research/2026-10-31-modshort-sort, 12 stages, REG/ILB native-equal) and a priority write-watch (research/2026-10-31-const-priority-watch, 1 stage): constants and leaves are weighted per reference group by a loop-nesting multiplier (SHCMDL 0x415a45..0x415b9b; 1 outside syntactic loops), physical registers go lowest-free in sort order, so ROM's order is f_2bf58, sel, 0, 320, g_606006c, 64 with f_2c0d0 left out, while the draft ranks f_2c0d0 (4 refs) over 64 (3). Inner while loops (research/2026-10-31-textmenu-inner-while) weight 64 into a register but hoist to a preheader like for loops (782 bytes, rejected); do-while loops entered at their condition (research/2026-10-31-textmenu-inner-do) avoid the preheader but register d_3aa9c and g_60792dc too (786 bytes, rejected). A do-while j loop alone (research/2026-10-31-textmenu-j-do) registers 64 and leaves f_2c0d0 out as ROM, but moves every leaf/constant def to the function entry (790 bytes, 156/404 exact, rejected); do-while outer, i and j loops (research/2026-10-31-textmenu-all-do) hoist all defs ahead of the wait loop (784 bytes, rejected). Any syntactic loop inside the pass pulls defs to the entry, so ROM's loops are all non-syntactic and its 64-over-f_2c0d0 ranking must come from reference counts, not loop weights. Constant-candidate trace (research/2026-10-31-const-count-trace, 1 stage): priority sums per-block groups, a constant used twice in one block counts 2, and webs need priority >= 2; the draft's button masks are single AND references (priority 1), yet ROM keeps 16/32 in r8 and copies b before testing 0x80/0x10, so its masks are referenced twice. (b & K) == K (research/2026-10-31-textmenu-mask-eq) compiles to and/cmp/eq rather than ROM tst: rejected. An inline button helper held(unsigned char b, unsigned char m) (research/2026-10-31-textmenu-button-helper, -int): a short return adds and/exts.w/tst per test (820 bytes); an int return gives exactly 808 bytes and 335/404 register-blind opcodes but and+tst per test (ROM folds to one tst after copying b), b registered in r12 (ROM r5) and 64 still immediate, because the constant parameter is propagated. Both rejected; modshort.c remains the best draft (220/404 exact). Accepted C shows the copy-then-tst idiom only when the mask is a register constant web and the left operand stays live (hud_ranges_f958 0x10f5c: mov r4,r2; tst r8,r2 with r8 = constant 1 web), so ROM's 0x80/0x10 tests prove those masks were webs (two counted references each); 0x40 and 0x20 skip the copy where the mask or b dies at the test. ROM also keeps one load of g_6079304 for the 0x80..0x20 tests and reloads for the final 14 test after the g_60792dc stores, consistent with CSE of *buttons loads. Unmerged centring arms solved: research/2026-10-18-nephele-bg-resource-count/resource_count.c writes sibling f_d962 with #pragma inline static short center_dbe8(char *s, short y) { return f_2bf58(...); } (646 bytes, 292/323 address-normalised instructions equal to ROM). The same returning helper in f_e074 (research/2026-10-31-textmenu-return-helper, 8 stages, confirmed) gives each sel==2 arm its own f_2c0d0/f_2bf58 calls as ROM: 810 bytes, raw 500, 222/404 exact (current best). Every void helper or expression form is merged. Native sort capture of rethelper.c (research/2026-10-31-rethelper-sort, 12 stages, native-equal): profit = priority - floor(clash sum / clash count); 64 is 3 - floor(130/33) = 0 and stays unregistered, f_2c0d0 and 320 are 4 - floor(122/31) = 1 (r8, r9). ROM's order needs one more counted 64 reference or f_2c0d0's clash sum >= 124. Whole-unit context matters (zero compiles): the same rethelper f_e074 compiled inside the rebased settings unit (research/2026-10-31-settings-e074-literals) differs in 52 instructions from its text_palette_e3b8 build and scores 263/404 address-normalised exact against ROM (vs 222 standalone), e.g. the entry sel=0 becomes an immediate as in ROM. f_e074 therefore has to be matched inside the full unit, and its admission depends on the same unit layout and .rodata ownership as f_bc02.
